text:
maria: heads-up — ran a cluster perf sweep with fused-attn (QKV packing + bias/rope epilogue) on the paged-KV workload and hit a regression on long-context traces. p99 jumped from ~24ms -> ~87ms when prefetch+epilogue-fuse were both enabled. logs attached below.

ow: repro command I used: `./bench --model llama-13b --seq 4096 --paged-kv --prefetch --fuse-epilogue --pack-qkv`

maria: quick excerpt from the run:
```
[bench] mode=fused pack_size=48 prefetch=on paged_kv=on
[stats] tokens=120k p50=12ms p95=36ms p99=87ms gpu_util=83% l2-misses=high
[warning] kernel_epilogue: stall cycles increase after step ~180
```

ow: hmm. did you try disabling only prefetch or only epilogue fuse to isolate?

maria: yes — turning off epilogue-fuse brings p99 back to ~26ms. turning off prefetch also helps slightly (~30ms) but best is epilogue off. suspicion: prefetch+epilogue reorder is causing page thrash for paged-KV paths.

ow: can you paste the flamegraph link?

maria: uploaded flame: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/2116001234 (filtered by hot kernels). Shows a big spike in `epilogue_pack_48` around the same region.

ci-bot: perf-job #211600-5 finished — baseline vs current: regressions detected in `fused_attn_epilogue` (p99 +3.5x). Full report: https://ci.redwood/jobs/211600-5/report

ken: thanks for the signal. quick thought — our kernel chooser currently prefers epilogue-fused variant when pack_size matches target lanes. For paged-KV the effective memory stride can vary per request which may invalidate the prefetch heuristics. We should add a guard that disables epilogue fusion for paged-kv when stride variance > threshold.

lili: I can run microbench on single-GPU with synthetic stride variance to reproduce locally. will try pack_size 32/48/64 and toggles.

maria: cool — I also sketched a small repro harness in `perf/bench/paged_kv_repro.py`. steps: 1) start paged-kv server with small page_size, 2) run bench with `--seed 43 --variance 0.25`. should hit the regression in ~2-3 runs.

ow: if this is really a prefetch ordering issue we might be able to fix in runtime by making prefetch operate on contiguous NVMe pages rather than kernel-internal fused blobs. cheaper patch: kernel chooser fallback for paged-kv.

maria: opened draft PR: https://git.redwood/p/perf/fused-epilogue-pagedkv-guard (WIP). patch adds runtime flag `runtime.disable_epilogue_for_paged_kv=true` and a chooser check. comments welcome.

ken: once lili confirms local repro, let's add a CI microbench that runs with small page sizes on merge. also add a telemetry metric for epilogue stall cycles so we can detect this automatically.

lili: reproed locally with your harness — confirmed. I'll attach the microbench numbers in the PR later today. (emoji: :white_check_mark:)

maria: thanks all. plan: lili uploads microbench -> ken + owen review quick fallback change -> merge gated by perf CI. I'll also add a note in runtime docs about disabling epilogue fusion for paged-kv workloads until we have a robust prefetch ordering.

ow: nice. can we add an opt-in knob to enable aggressive prefetch for dedicated clusters only? might be useful for perf-hungry customers.

maria: good idea — I'll put that in a follow-up.

ci-bot: note: job #211600-6 scheduled to run benchmarks with `runtime.disable_epilogue_for_paged_kv=true` on canary cluster.
